records.text: The BIS Annual Economic Report lays out the "next-generation monetary system": stablecoins fail the three tests of money — singleness, elasticity, integrity — and the future is a tokenized unified ledger anchored in central-bank money. The tower of central banks publishes its counter-manifesto five weeks before GENIUS is signed.

records.title: Project Pine — the New York Fed and the BIS Innovation Hub, with the ECB, Bank of England and four others — proves central banks can run monetary policy in a fully tokenized system …
records.text: Project Pine — the New York Fed and the BIS Innovation Hub, with the ECB, Bank of England and four others — proves central banks can run monetary policy in a fully tokenized system: interest on reserves, asset purchases, collateral calls, all by smart contract. The central banks aren't fighting the ledger; they're learning to drive it.

records.title: The ECON committee adopts the digital euro framework 43 to 14 — holding caps reviewed every two years, privacy-by-design, a 24-month rollout — and orders trilogues.
records.text: The ECON committee adopts the digital euro framework 43 to 14 — holding caps reviewed every two years, privacy-by-design, a 24-month rollout — and orders trilogues. The stated purpose, in the headline itself: reduce US dominance in payments. The last big parliamentary hurdle falls the same day Basel doubles down on stablecoins.

records.text: The ECB closes the digital euro preparation phase and moves to the next stage: pilot transactions targeted for mid-2027, possible issuance 2029 — all contingent on the regulation passing in 2026. While every other retail CBDC on Earth retreats, the euro's marches forward.

records.text: Bloomberg: the Bank and Treasury are discussing converting this summer's promised go/no-go on the digital pound into a suspension — internal research shows the benefit of a retail CBDC shrinking while banks prove out tokenized deposits. Another retail state ledger quietly dies in committee.
